subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat `all | final | off` tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should apply to failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the remaining gap, but adding this policy creates public config and decides whether UX suppression may override the current visible warning fallback for failed side effects.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or channel-specific leak fixes.

options.title: Split by warning family
options.body: Defer a general enum and track remaining leaks, routing needs, or channel aggregates in narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the warning-policy fixes and related PRs explicitly separated this issue as the broader delivery-policy follow-up.
